question: Do the PEMSEA/ASEANO Imus River reports supply fish taxa or an adoptable watershed boundary, and what source gaps remain?

sourceReviews.title: The situation and causes of plastic pollution in the Imus River, Cavite
sourceReviews.access: Official PEMSEA publication page and online PDF text reviewed; no local binary retained.

findings.fishStudyStatement: The report states that a detailed study of Imus River had not yet been conducted at the time of publication.
findings.adjacentWatershedFishContext: The report mentions fewer than 20 identified fish species across nearby watershed studies named as Cañas, Pasong Camachile, and Timalan, alongside shrimp and crab. It provides no fish names, study-level list, station, date, or allocation to Imus River or any one named neighboring river.
findings.aquacultureContext: A separate statement reports 148 metric tons of fish and prawns annually for the combined Imus-Ylang-Ylang-Rio Grande water-quality-management-area drainage basin, with aquaculture pens in some rivers. This is combined aquaculture context, not a wild-fish inventory or an Imus River occurrence record.
findings.sourceReportedDimensions: The report describes Imus River as 36.7 km long with a 168.1 km2 drainage basin; these are report-era narrative measurements, not adopted geometry.

sourceReviews.title: ASEANO Project Report: Mapping and Characterization of the Imus River Watershed
sourceReviews.access: Official publication page and full online PDF text reviewed; no local binary or spatial data file retained.

findings.methodAndExtent: The report says it delineated the watershed using a 5-meter-resolution Cavite digital elevation model and mapped physical, topographic, stream, land-cover, and hydroclimatic characteristics.
findings.sourceReportedDimensions: It reports a watershed area of 11,259.80 hectares, 56 perennial streams with 186.15 km total length, and 36 river segments. It also cites a 38.4 km main Imus River length from a separate Cavite Ecological Profile source.
findings.fishEvidence: No fish species checklist or fish sampling results were found in the reviewed report text; the term fish appears in map land-use context for fish ponds, not as a wild-fish survey.
findings.spatialData: The PDF contains watershed and river-network maps, but a downloadable vector boundary, channel geometry, CRS for an exportable dataset, and item-specific reuse permission were not located. No geometry was digitized from the PDF figures.

sourceReviews.title: Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed
sourceReviews.access: Official CvSU Research Center listing reviewed; the underlying project report and dataset were not located in the bounded search.

findings.interpretation: The listing confirms an Imus River watershed project and project dates, but does not describe fish methods, sites, taxa, or a report download. Treat it as a follow-up research lead only.

crossReportComparison.areaAndLength: The 2020 baseline reports 168.1 km2 and 36.7 km for its drainage-basin/river narrative; the 2022 mapping report reports 11,259.80 ha and cites a 38.4 km main channel, while separately reporting a 186.15 km network. The reports do not reconcile their area definitions or channel-length measurements. Preserve the source-specific values; do not choose one as a validated boundary or trace.
crossReportComparison.fishAttribution: Neither report provides species-level evidence for Imus River. The 2020 report's nearby-watershed summary and combined aquaculture figure are not transferred to Imus River or to a particular neighboring waterbody.

rightsReview.decision: Retain bibliographic metadata and minimal factual research summaries only. Do not reproduce report wording, maps, figures, underlying GIS, or fish lists without item-specific rights confirmation.

limits: The 2020 statement that no detailed Imus River study existed is limited to the authors' knowledge at publication time; it does not establish the absence of later studies.
The adjacent-watershed fish summary has no species names, methods, stations, dates, or waterbody-by-taxon crosswalk.
Watershed boundaries are land-drainage areas and must not be substituted for the river channel or legal fishing-water boundaries.
No current fish presence, absence, catchability, diet, water safety, fishing access, or legal advice is established.
nextAction: Locate the full report or deliverables for CvSU’s listed 2020-11 to 2021-04 Imus River biophysical-characterization project through a public library/repository route. Verify whether it contains fish sampling, named sites, dates, methods, taxa, and item-specific reuse terms. Separately seek an official or openly licensed vector watershed/channel dataset; do not infer results or submit a request without separate authorization.

sources.supports: Official publication metadata for the July 2020 Imus River baseline report.
2020 report full-text statements about the historical fish-study gap, unassigned neighboring-watershed fish summary, combined aquaculture context, and narrative dimensions.
Official publication metadata and description for the April 2022 watershed-mapping report.
2022 report full-text methods, source-reported watershed area and stream network, and reviewed map/data limitations.

Official CvSU Research Center project listing for the 2020-11 to 2021-04 Imus River watershed biophysical-characterization project; no underlying fish report or dataset is linked in the reviewed record.

queries: site:edu.ph Imus River fish biodiversity Cavite
"Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed"
boundedPostPublicationSearch.outcome: The bounded public search surfaced an official CvSU Research Center entry for the 2020-11 to 2021-04 biophysical-characterization project, but not its full report or fish-specific results. Other Imus hits were watershed mapping, pollution or water-quality monitoring, including a Pseudomonas microbiology study; these do not provide a wild-fish species inventory.
limits: This is a time-bounded web-index search, not a complete search of CvSU library holdings, internal project files, unpublished reports, theses, or local-government archives.
Failure to locate an indexed report does not establish that fish sampling did not occur or that fish are absent.
Water-quality observations and microbial species are separate evidence from fish presence or a fish checklist.
